decisions.summary: Combined-total construction (closest, answer 4). Solve-test: A alone yields one leader, B two, C one; no view reaches the total. A+B gives three leaders but cannot confirm C holds no fourth; A+C gives two but cannot confirm B; B+C likewise. Only the full A/B/C view sums to the four jonin sensei (Kakashi, Kurenai, Asuma, Guy). The 2+1 partitions {A,B}|{C} and {A,C}|{B} both leave the pair short of the answer.

Filtered-count with a distributed rule (multiple_choice, answer 1). Solve-test: A names two Sannin summons, B names one, C alone holds the counting rule. A+B has every candidate but no rule, so it cannot filter; A+C and B+C have the rule but only a partial candidate set, so neither can produce a confident total. Only combining the rule (C) with all three summons pins the snake-summoning Sannin (Orochimaru). All merge partitions leave the pair unable to solve.

Relative-ordering construction (match, answer Kokuo / Five-Tails). Solve-test: A holds {1}, B holds {9}, C holds the ordering rule plus {5}. Any two values leave the middle ambiguous (e.g. {5,9} could be ordered with a missing value below 5, between, or above 9). Only the full {1,5,9} pins the middle to 5, identifying Kokuo. The answer name appears in no segment, so no leakage. All merges leave the pair without the complete triple.
